{{short description|American mathematician & academic}}
'''Jacqueline Ann Jensen-Vallin''' is an American mathematician. She is a chair and professor of mathematics at [[Lamar University]],{{r|cv}} former [[editor-in-chief]] of ''[[MAA FOCUS]]'', the newsletter of the [[Mathematical Association of America]] (MAA),{{r|focus}} and a former governor of the Texas Section of the MAA.{{r|gov}} Her research interests include [[combinatorial group theory]], [[low-dimensional topology]], and [[knot theory]];{{r|cv}} she is also known for her work in [[mathematics education]] and the history of [[women in mathematics]].

==Education and career==
Jensen-Vallin did her undergraduate studies at the [[University of Connecticut]], completing a [[double major]] in mathematics and psychology in 1995.{{r|cv}} She went to the [[University of Oregon]] for her graduate studies, and completed her doctorate there in 2002. Her dissertation, ''Finding <math>\pi_2</math>-Generators for Exotic Homotopy Types of Two-Complexes'', concerned [[algebraic geometry]] and was supervised by Micheal Dyer.{{r|cv|mgp}}

After completing her doctorate, she joined the faculty at [[Sam Houston State University]] in 2002. She moved to Lamar University in 2014.

==Book==
With [[Janet Beery]], Sarah J. Greenwald, and Maura B. Mast, Jensen-Vallin is an editor of the book ''Women in Mathematics: Celebrating the Centennial of the Mathematical Association of America'' (Springer, 2017).<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Quertermous |first1=Katie Spurrier |title=Women in Mathematics: A Review by Katie Spurrier Quertermous |journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |date=March 2019 |volume=66 |issue=3 |pages=395–398 |doi=10.1090/noti1861  |doi-access=free|s2cid=127156649 |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/201903/rnoti-p395.pdf}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Jensen-Vallin was one of the 2008 winners of the Henry L. Alder Award for Distinguished Teaching by a Beginning College or University Mathematics Faculty Member.{{r|alder}}

The [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] gave her their Service Award in 2018.{{r|cv}}<ref>{{cite web |title=AWM Service Award |url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-service-award/ |website=Association for Women in Mathematics |accessdate=26 August 2019}}</ref>
